svg.text: VX_ptw_walker — one level-counted walk, and the walk cache that lets it skip to the leaf table
The same four-state machine walks Sv32 (2 levels, 4-byte PTE) and Sv39 (3 levels, 8-byte PTE); the geometry comes from the VX_VM_* contract, the level from a counter.
Walker state machine (per walker, NUM_WALKERS independent copies)
IDLE
req_ready = 1
REQ
mem req_valid
WAIT
mem rsp_ready
RESP
rsp_valid
dispatch: latch id, vpn,
base_ppn, level
req fire: pte_sel
latched
rsp fire, non-leaf, level > 0: base_ppn ← pte.ppn, level ← level − 1
rsp fire ∧ walk_done:
result ← {pte.ppn, flags,
level, walk_fault}
rsp_ready:
result → rsp arb
pte_addr = {base_ppn, vpn[level·LEVEL_BITS +: LEVEL_BITS] << PTE_SHIFT} (one PTE per level)
pte = rsp.data[pte_sel·PTE_W +: PTE_W] pte_sel = pte_addr[WORD_SHIFT-1:PTE_SHIFT]
leaf = R|W|X bad = ¬V ∨ (¬R∧W) misaligned = pte.ppn & ((1 << level·LEVEL_BITS) − 1) ≠ 0
walk_fault — the only faults a walker raises
walk_fault = bad ∨ (leaf ∧ misaligned) ∨ (¬leaf ∧ level == 0)
walk_done = walk_fault ∨ leaf
A faulting walk still answers its miss-station slot (fault=1, nothing installed), so every
parked requester is killed rather than left waiting. The same cycle, fault_if pulses once with
{va = vpn ≪ PAGE_LOG2, access, amo} as recorded at dispatch; VX_mmu_dcr latches the first.
Permission (R/W/X/U) is never judged here: a walk is shared by requests of differing intent.
VX_ptw_cache — direct-mapped last-level table pointers (WALK_CACHE_SIZE entries)
tag = vpn[VPN_W-1 : LEVEL_BITS] (the VPN with its last-level index stripped)
idx = tag[IDX_W-1 : 0] IDX_W = clog2(WALK_CACHE_SIZE)
hit = valid[idx] ∧ tag_r[idx] == tag → start_ppn = ppn_r[idx], start_level = 0
miss → start_ppn = satp.PPN, start_level = PT_LEVELS − 1
Written by any walker the cycle its walk steps from level 1 into level 0: {tag(vpn) → pte.ppn}.
At most one write per cycle (lowest walker index wins). Cleared on every flush_if.req.
Effect: a walk whose 4 KB neighbours were recently walked costs one PTE fetch instead of
PT_LEVELS — two on Sv32, three on Sv39. The saving grows with the depth of the table.
Probed combinationally on the incoming miss (miss_if.req_data.vpn) so the walker is
dispatched already pointed at the right table. Only interior tables are cached; a
superpage leaf found above level 0 is returned with its level and never cached here.
PT_LEVELS == 1 disables the probe (wc_use gated) — there is no interior level to skip.
Walker pool and its ports (VX_ptw)
Dispatch
miss_if.req_ready = ∃ idle walker; the lowest idle
index takes the request. dispatch_i latches the
request's vpn / access / amo for the fault report.
No queue in front of the pool: a full pool back-
pressures the cluster TLB's issue buffer, which
holds the request. Walkers are independent, so
NUM_WALKERS walks overlap their PTE latency.
PTE fetch port
VX_mem_bus_arb NUM_WALKERS→1, round-robin; the walker index is
appended to the tag (TAG_SEL_IDX) so responses demux back.
REQ_OUT_BUF=3: the port leaves the PTW fully registered.
DATA_SIZE = L1 line: one line read per level, PTE word selected
by pte_sel; rw=0, byteen all ones, attr=0 (cacheable, no bypass).
Attached to the shared L2 as client L2_PTW_IDX — PTEs are cached
like data, and repeat walks of a hot table hit in the L2.
Response and fault
VX_stream_arb NUM_WALKERS→1 (round-robin, OUT_BUF=2) returns
{id, fault, level, ppn, flags} to the cluster TLB's miss station.
A response that fires with fault=1 also drives fault_if for one
cycle (lowest faulting walker wins if two coincide).
empty = no walker active; flush_if.done = req ∧ empty. An in-flight
walk is never aborted: the flush waits for it, and its fill lands
in a miss station that is itself waiting to clear on empty.
